number.why: The reported RR is 1.04 with 95% CI 0.84–1.28 for AAD including CDD, comparing the microbial preparation with placebo. This is the modified intention-to-treat analysis of AAD within 8 weeks of recruitment, matching the served row. Agreement does not establish the generic served_outcome labels of intention-to-treat and study end; the ruling already identifies that discrepancy.

quotes.span: AAD (including CDD) occurred in 159 (10·8%) participants in the microbial preparation group and 153 (10·4%) participants in the placebo group (relative risk [RR] 1·04; 95% CI 0·84-1·28; p=0·71).
The primary outcomes were occurrence of AAD within 8 weeks and C difficile diarrhoea (CDD) within 12 weeks of recruitment. Analysis was by modified intention-to-treat.

entry.why: The trial directly establishes antibiotic exposure in older hospital inpatients and randomisation to a probiotic preparation or placebo. This population falls within the question's patients receiving antibiotics.

quotes.span: We did a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, pragmatic, efficacy trial of inpatients aged 65 years and older and exposed to one or more oral or parenteral antibiotics.

We have designed a prospective, parallel group trial where people aged 65 years or more admitted to hospital and receiving one or more antibiotics are randomly allocated to receive either one capsule of the probiotic or a matching placebo daily for 21 days.

missed: No additional finding changes either verdict. The analysis-population and timepoint discrepancies were already acknowledged in the ruling.
